en: to burn; to be burnt; to be scorched

examples.en: This paper burns well.
The meat is so burnt that I can't eat it.
I smell something burning somewhere.

examples.ko: 불이 나서 오래된 집이 다 탔어요.
examples.en: There was a fire, and the old house burned down completely.
If the heat is too high, the rice burns.

examples.ko: 난로 안에서 숯이 빨갛게 타고 있어요.
examples.en: Charcoal is burning red inside the stove.

explain: '타다'는 '불이 붙어 타다', '음식이 눌어 타다' 모두에 써요. 내가 불을 붙이거나 실수로 음식을 태우면 '태우다'를 써서 '고기를 태웠어요'라고 해요. 소리가 같은 '타다'(탈것을 타다, 음료를 타다)는 함께 쓰는 말로 구별해요.

phrases.example: 연락이 없어서 하루 종일 애가 탔어요.
phrases.en: to be worried sick; to be on edge
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정이나 초조함 때문에 마음이 몹시 불안할 때 써요. 뭔가를 애타게 기다릴 때 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are very anxious or worried and can't relax. It is often said when you are waiting anxiously for something.

explain_en: Basic word for something catching fire or getting scorched. '타다' is used both for something catching fire and for food getting burnt. When someone burns something, whether on purpose or by mistake, you use '태우다', as in '고기를 태웠어요'. It sounds the same as the other '타다' words (riding, mixing a drink), so tell them apart by the words around it.

examples.en: It's delicious to wrap meat in a perilla leaf and eat it.
We grow perilla leaves on our balcony.
What did you plant in the garden? Chili peppers and perilla.
I bought a bunch of perilla leaves at the market.

explain: 영어로 sesame leaf라고 옮기지만 실제로는 들깨의 잎이에요. 쌈, 장아찌, 전, 김치로 먹고 향이 강해서 좋아하는 사람과 싫어하는 사람이 나뉘어요. 발음은 [깬닙]이에요.

phrases.en: I wrapped rice and meat in perilla leaves and ate it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깻잎에 음식을 싸 먹는 쌈을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A wrap made by wrapping food in perilla leaves.

phrases.example: 깻잎 향이 좋아서 자꾸 먹게 돼요.
phrases.en: The perilla leaf scent is so good that I keep eating it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깻잎의 강한 냄새를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the strong aroma of perilla leaves.

phrases.en: My mother made perilla leaf pancakes for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깻잎으로 만든 전 요리를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pan-fried dish made with perilla leaves.

explain_en: It is often translated as 'sesame leaf', but it is actually the leaf of the perilla plant (들깨). It is eaten as a wrap, pickle, in pancakes and as kimchi, and its strong scent divides people. The pronunciation is [깬닙].

examples.en: This morning I spread strawberry jam on bread and ate it.
I received a jar of strawberry jam as a gift.
We also sell homemade strawberry jam.
Keep the strawberry jam in the refrigerator.
I like grape jam better than strawberry jam.
We've run out of strawberry jam, so I need to go to the supermarket.

explain: 잼은 빵에 '바르다'와 함께 써요. 표준 표기는 '잼'이라서 '쨈'이라고 쓰지 않아요. 병으로 사기 때문에 '한 병'으로 세요.

phrases.en: I spread strawberry jam on the bread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잼은 빵에 '바르다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Jam goes with 바르다 (to spread) on bread.

phrases.en: My mom made strawberry jam from strawberries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 직접 만든다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when someone makes jam at home.

phrases.en: I packed a strawberry jam sandwich for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잼을 넣은 음식 이름으로 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be used as the name of a food made with jam.

explain_en: Jam goes with the verb '바르다' (to spread) on bread. The standard spelling is '잼', not '쨈'. It is sold in jars, so you count it as '한 병'.

examples.en: Two fried shrimp, please.
I dipped the fried shrimp in sauce and ate it.
The fried shrimp cooled down and got soggy.
The fried shrimp rice bowl is the tastiest.
Shall we have fried shrimp for dinner tonight?

explain: 튀김은 '야채튀김', '오징어튀김'처럼 재료 이름 뒤에 붙여요. 분식집에서 '튀김'을 주문하면 이런 종류가 나와요. 맛을 말할 때는 '바삭하다'가 가장 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: The crispy fried shrimp is really delicious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 맛을 말할 때 '바삭하다'를 활용해서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 'basakhada' (crispy) to describe the taste, a very common pairing.

phrases.en: I ordered fried shrimp at the snack shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당이나 분식집에서 음식을 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering food at a restaurant or snack shop.

phrases.example: 여기 새우튀김 한 접시 더 주세요.
phrases.en: One more plate of fried shrimp, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식당에서 양을 말하며 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering a portion at a restaurant.

explain_en: '튀김' is attached after the ingredient, as in '야채튀김' and '오징어튀김'. At a snack shop, ordering '튀김' gets you assorted items like these. To describe its taste, '바삭하다' (crispy) fits best.

examples.en: In winter I eat fish cake on the street.
The fish cake broth is warm and tasty.
I boiled a soup with radish and fish cake in it.
I bought a bag of fish cake at the market.
I packed stir-fried fish cake as a side dish in the lunch box.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 일본어에서 온 '오뎅'이라는 말도 아직 많이 들려요. 하지만 표준어는 '어묵'이에요. 꼬치에 꽂아 국물에 끓인 길거리 음식을 말할 때 '오뎅'을 쓰는 사람이 많고, 반찬이나 국에 넣는 재료는 '어묵'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I had an odeng on my way home from work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 말에서 많이 들리지만 표준어는 '어묵'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often heard in everyday talk, but the standard word is 어묵.

phrases.en: I drank a cup of fish cake broth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길거리 어묵을 먹을 때 국물도 같이 마셔요.
phrases.nuance_en: People drink the broth along with street fish cakes.

phrases.en: Two fish cake skewers, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼬치에 꽂은 어묵은 '개'로 세어 주문해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Skewered fish cakes are ordered by number with 개.

explain_en: In everyday talk you still often hear 오뎅, a word borrowed from Japanese, but the standard word is 어묵. Many people say 오뎅 for the skewered street food simmered in broth, and 어묵 for the ingredient in side dishes and soups.

examples.en: In the hot summer, I think of patbingsu.

examples.ko: 우리 팥빙수 하나 시켜서 나눠 먹어요.
examples.en: Let's order one patbingsu and share it.
This cafe is famous for its strawberry patbingsu.

examples.ko: 팥빙수를 너무 빨리 먹으면 머리가 아파요.
examples.en: If you eat patbingsu too fast, you get a headache.

examples.ko: 할머니가 만들어 주신 팥빙수가 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The patbingsu my grandmother made for me is the tastiest.

explain: [팓삥수]처럼 소리 나요. 얼음 위에 단팥을 올린 여름 디저트라서 '먹기 전에 잘 비벼요'라고 말하는 일이 많고, 과일을 올리면 '과일빙수'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Shaved ice is delicious in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팥이 없는 것까지 두루 말하는 넓은 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A broader word that also covers kinds without red beans.

phrases.en: One patbingsu here, please.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카페나 식당에서 주문할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when ordering at a cafe or restaurant.

phrases.en: I mix the patbingsu well and eat it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먹기 전에 섞는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes mixing it before eating.

explain_en: It is pronounced [팓삥수]. It is a summer dessert with sweet red beans on shaved ice, and people often say to mix it well before eating. With fruit on top it can be called '과일빙수'.

examples.ko: 두꺼운 겨울옷은 옷장 맨 위 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The thick winter clothes are on the top shelf of the closet.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 겨울옷도 꼭 챙기세요.
examples.en: Be sure to pack winter clothes too when you travel.
I haven't put away my winter clothes yet.
I dressed my child in a thick jacket as winter wear.

explain: 반대말은 '여름옷'이에요. 계절이 바뀔 때 '겨울옷 정리', '겨울옷을 꺼내다'처럼 자주 말해요. '겨울 옷'처럼 띄어 쓰지 않고 한 낱말로 써요.

phrases.en: It got cold, so I took out my winter clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨울이 시작될 때 옷장에서 옷을 꺼내는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when taking winter clothes out of storage as winter begins.

phrases.en: When spring comes, I put away my winter clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계절이 바뀔 때 옷을 정리하는 일을 짧게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short phrase for sorting winter clothes when the season changes.

phrases.en: It's cold outside, so I wore thick winter clothes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨울옷의 두께를 말할 때 '두꺼운'을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 두꺼운 describes how thick the clothes are.

explain_en: The opposite is '여름옷'. When the seasons change, people often say '겨울옷 정리' or '겨울옷을 꺼내다'. It is written as one word, '겨울옷', without a space.

examples.en: Not the short-sleeved shirt, please give me the long-sleeved one.

explain: 반대말은 '긴소매'예요. 일상에서는 '반팔'이라고도 많이 말해요. 옷은 '입다'와 함께 써서 '반소매를 입다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I wear short sleeves a lot in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반소매'와 같은 뜻이고 일상에서 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 반소매 and more common in daily speech.

phrases.en: I bought a short-sleeved T-shirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷 이름 앞에 붙여 어떤 옷인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a clothing name to describe it.

phrases.en: It's warm today, so I wore short sleeves.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷은 '입다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Clothes go with the verb 입다.

explain_en: Sleeves ending around the upper arm (반소매 옷) The opposite is '긴소매'. In everyday talk people also say '반팔'. It goes with '입다', as in '반소매를 입다'.

en: to be on vacation; to close for a vacation

examples.en: Our school goes on vacation next week.
Our school started vacation at the end of July.
When school breaks for vacation, I'll go to my hometown.
The kids are very excited because vacation starts tomorrow.
I took photos with my friends before vacation started.
It has been a week since vacation started.

explain: 주어는 학교나 학생이고, 직장인이 쉬는 건 '방학'이 아니라 '휴가'예요. 방학이 끝나고 학교가 다시 시작하는 건 '개학하다'라서 둘이 짝이에요. '방학 동안'처럼 명사 '방학'을 더 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I will study Korean during the vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방학이 이어지는 기간을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the period while the vacation lasts.

phrases.en: School starts again next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방학이 끝나고 학교가 다시 시작할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The paired word for school starting again after vacation.

phrases.en: My school is on vacation now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 방학 중이라는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of being on vacation right now.

explain_en: The subject is a school or students; office workers take '휴가' (leave), not 방학. When vacation ends and school starts again, you say '개학하다', so the two are a pair. The noun appears more often, as in '방학 동안' (during the break).

en: to make a mistake; to make a slip

examples.en: Everyone makes mistakes sometimes.
It's okay to make mistakes at first.
You must not make mistakes when calculating.

explain: '틀리다'는 답이 맞지 않다는 결과이고, '실수하다'는 아는 것을 부주의로 잘못했을 때 써요. '실수로 넘어졌어요'처럼 '실수로'를 붙이면 일부러 한 게 아니라는 말이 돼요. 정말 큰 잘못은 '잘못하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I broke my friend's cup by mistake.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 한 게 아니라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the meaning that it was not done on purpose.

phrases.en: Don't make mistakes on the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심하라고 당부할 때 쓰는 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to urge someone to be careful.

phrases.en: I made a small mistake in my presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '실수하다'를 '실수 + 를 하다'로 나눠 쓴 말로, '작은 실수'처럼 꾸밀 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb split as '실수 + 를 하다', which lets you add words like 'small'.

explain_en: General everyday word for any careless mistake or slip. '틀리다' describes a wrong result, such as a wrong answer, while 실수하다 is slipping up on something you actually know because you weren't careful. Adding '실수로' ('by mistake') shows you didn't do it on purpose. For a real wrongdoing, use '잘못하다'.

en: to become disgusted with; to get sick of

examples.ko: 친구가 거짓말을 한 뒤로 그 친구가 싫어졌어요.
examples.en: After my friend lied, I started to dislike that friend.

explain: '싫다'는 지금의 마음이고, '싫어지다'는 좋았거나 괜찮았던 것이 싫게 변했다는 뜻이에요. 반대말은 '좋아지다'예요. 같은 것을 너무 많이 해서 질릴 때는 '질리다'라고도 하는데, '싫어지다'는 음식·일뿐 아니라 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I suddenly started to dislike that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 이미 변했다는 것을 과거형으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense, saying the change of heart has already happened.

phrases.en: I started to get sick of studying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싫은 마음이 조금씩 생기는 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the moment when the dislike begins to grow.

phrases.en: No matter how much I eat, I never get sick of kimchi.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계속 해도 질리지 않는다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you don't get tired of something even when you keep doing it.

explain_en: '싫다' is a present feeling, while '싫어지다' means something you liked or tolerated turned into something you dislike. The opposite is '좋아지다'. When you tire of something from overdoing it, '질리다' is also used, but '싫어지다' can be used for people as well as food or work.

examples.en: The cost of books is separate from tuition.
I borrow books from the library to save on book costs.

examples.ko: 책값 때문에 사고 싶은 책을 못 샀어요.
examples.en: I couldn't buy the book I wanted because of the price.
My older sister paid for the books for me.

examples.ko: 등록금에 책값까지 합치면 돈이 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Tuition plus book costs adds up to a lot of money.

explain: '책값이 오르다/내리다', '책값을 내다'처럼 써요. '밥값', '차비'처럼 어떤 것을 사는 데 드는 돈을 나타내는 '-값' 표현 중 하나예요. 한 단어로 붙여 쓰는 점도 알아 두세요.

phrases.en: Books at university cost too much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책의 가격이 높다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that the price of books is high.

phrases.en: My friend paid for my book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책 사는 데 드는 돈을 지불할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when paying for a book.

phrases.en: Book prices go up every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가격이 비싸지는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when prices get higher.

explain_en: Say '책값이 오르다/내리다' (rise/fall) and '책값을 내다' (pay). It's one of the '-값' expressions for the money spent buying something, like '밥값'. Note that it is written as one word.

en: peal of thunder; sound of thunder

examples.en: I woke up at night because of the thunder.
The thunder was so loud that the child cried.
The sudden thunder startled me and I screamed.
Our puppy is afraid of the sound of thunder.
The sound of thunder is heard later than the lightning.

examples.ko: 비가 오면 천둥소리와 빗소리가 섞여 들려요.
examples.en: When it rains, thunder and rain sounds blend together.

explain: 소리를 말할 때는 '천둥소리가 나다/들리다', 현상을 말할 때는 '천둥이 치다'라고 해요. 번개는 '번개가 치다'로 같이 '치다'를 써요. 소리를 흉내 낸 말로는 '우르릉 쾅쾅'이 있어요.

phrases.en: Thunder rumbled all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천둥이 생기는 현상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the thunder itself happening.

phrases.en: There was a sudden clap of thunder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리가 생긴 것에 집중해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the sound occurring.

phrases.en: I can hear thunder in the distance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내 귀에 소리가 들어올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the sound reaches your ears.

explain_en: Everyday spoken word; thunder noise. For the sound, say '천둥소리가 나다/들리다'; for the event, '천둥이 치다'. Lightning also uses '치다', as in '번개가 치다'. A word imitating the sound is '우르릉 쾅쾅'.

t90.ax: I woke up at night because of the thunder.

examples.en: What do I do if the flight gets cancelled?
The reservation was cancelled, so I changed it to another day.
I got a text saying the class will be cancelled.

explain: 일정·예약·공연처럼 이미 정해진 일이 없던 일이 될 때 써요. 내가 직접 하면 '취소하다', 다른 이유로 그렇게 되면 '취소되다'예요. 약속이 갑자기 없어지는 일은 '펑크 나다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 비가 많이 오면 공연이 취소될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If it rains a lot, the show may be cancelled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 확실하지 않지만 취소될 가능성이 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when cancellation is possible but not certain.

phrases.en: The reservation wasn't cancelled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취소되지 않고 그대로 있다는 뜻의 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form meaning it is still on.

phrases.en: My plan with my friend suddenly fell through.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속이 갑자기 없어질 때 쓰는 편한 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way to say a plan suddenly fell through.

explain_en: Use it when something already planned, like a schedule, booking, or show, falls through. If you do it yourself it is 취소하다; if it happens for some other reason it is 취소되다. A plan that suddenly falls through is also called 펑크 나다 in casual speech.

examples.en: My glasses keep sliding down to the tip of my nose.
The cat lightly licked the tip of my nose.

examples.ko: 코끝에 땀이 맺힐 만큼 열심히 뛰었어요.
examples.en: I ran so hard that sweat beaded on the tip of my nose.

explain: '코'가 얼굴의 코 전체라면 '코끝'은 맨 끝부분만 콕 집어 말해요. 추워서 빨개지거나 시릴 때, 냄새가 스칠 때처럼 코끝에서 느끼는 감각을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I got choked up while reading the letter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 슬프거나 감동해서 눈물이 날 것 같을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are so sad or moved that you feel close to tears.

explain_en: While '코' is the whole nose, '코끝' points to just the very tip. It fits sensations felt at the tip, such as the nose turning red or stinging from the cold, or a smell brushing past.
